research_notes: All patterns verified against named sources: Angler Adventures, Orvis/Deep Water Cay, Fish-Bones Grand Cayman (Cayman-specific), Flatsnation (Cayman Sleek), Global FlyFisher (Meko Special), SaltyFlyTying/Deneki (Andros/Bahamas), Xcalak on the Fly / Woolybuggin (Mexico Yucatan), Palometa Club (Ascension Bay), Fishing Adventures Bonaire (Bonaire flats), Soul Fly Lodge (Berry Islands/Bahamas). Originator dates omitted where year of origination is unverified.

regions.name: Bimini, Bahamas
regions.notes: Closest Bahamas island to Florida; home to some of the largest Atlantic bonefish on deep, clear sand flats. Flies need heavier eyes (lead or large bead-chain) to reach bottom on the 2-4 ft deep Bimini Sound flats. Big-profile patterns outperform small flies for the resident large bones.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Universal Bahamas staple — bead-chain eye weight and pearl/tan body match Bimini sand-flat shrimp and land softly enough for pressured fish.

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.notes: Arguably the single most-recommended Bahamas bonefish fly; pearl mylar body and pink nose excel on Bimini's light sand bottom in sizes #2-#4 for big fish.

patterns.name: Clouser Deep Minnow
patterns.notes: Tan-and-white Clouser with lead eyes is the go-to deep-water pattern when Bimini bones hold in 3-5 ft channels adjacent to the flats.

patterns.name: Bunny Bone
patterns.notes: Rabbit-fur skinny-water fly recommended by Angler Adventures for tailing fish in 6-18 inches; the soft landing is essential in calm Bimini Sound conditions.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.notes: Amber and tan Bitters is universally recommended for Bahamas clear-water flats and is an excellent neutral-profile option when fish are selective.

patterns.name: Meko Special
patterns.notes: Created by Grand Bahama guide Omeko Glinton; neutral tan body with palmered hackle works across dark and light bottoms without switching flies — well-suited to Bimini's mixed flats.

patterns.name: Craven's Bonefish Junk
patterns.notes: Evolved from the Gotcha with rubber legs, epoxy eyes, and a bright orange hotspot; large profile (#2-#4) appeals to Bimini's big, adult bones that key on size.

patterns.name: Del Brown's Permit Fly (Merkin)
patterns.notes: Standard permit crab for the occasional permit encountered on Bimini flats; also eaten by large bonefish feeding on crabs over grassy patches.

patterns.name: EP Ghost Shrimp
patterns.notes: Tan EP Ghost Shrimp recommended by Deep Water Cay guides for cautious Bahamas bonefish; very sparse profile lands quietly and sinks on bead-chain eyes.

patterns.name: Peterson's Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: High-confidence Bahamas pattern with reports of 19-fish days; rabbit-fur wing pulses at rest, effective on both Bimini bonefish and the occasional permit.

patterns.name: Christmas Island Special
patterns.notes: Recommended by Deep Water Cay guides (Orvis article) for quiet entry on spooky fish; gold or orange colorway works year-round on Bahamian sand.

patterns.name: Velcro Crab
patterns.notes: Top Bahamas permit crab called out by Deep Water Cay guides; presented ahead of cruising permit with a bottom-sinking drift, also taken by big bonefish.

patterns.name: Brewer's Amber Shrimp
patterns.notes: Classic Bahamas shrimp in amber/tan with wood-duck tail; listed by Angler Adventures as a must-have pattern for Bahamian flats including Bimini — amber colorway matches mangrove-edge shrimp.

patterns.name: Simram
patterns.notes: Lead-eye deep-water Bahamas pattern featured by Angler Adventures; the rabbit-strip wing and shrimp silhouette are effective when Bimini bones hold in deeper channel edges.

regions.name: Turks & Caicos
regions.notes: Large bonefish averaging 5-8 lb on Caicos Bank flats surrounding North and Middle Caicos. Less-pressured fishery than Bahamas; fish are willing but also encountered in diverse depth conditions from 6-inch tailwater to 3-ft cruising flats. Strong DIY wading scene (Provo, Bottle Creek).

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.notes: Explicitly recommended by The Sands resort and multiple T&C guides as the single best fly for Provo bonefish — tan and pink colorways in #2-#6.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Foundational T&C flat fly; bead-chain weight perfectly suited to 2-3 ft flats; pearl and tan variants cover sand and grass bottoms alike.

patterns.name: Veverka Mantis Shrimp
patterns.notes: Soft landing and realistic mantis-shrimp profile make it a top choice for cautious T&C fish; Soul Fly Lodge (Berry Islands) and Deep Water Cay guides both recommend it as a first-choice pattern.

patterns.name: EP Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: Listed as a top Bahamas/T&C flat fly by Soul Fly Lodge; EP fiber profile moves naturally in the water and sinks efficiently to the 2-4 ft Caicos Bank depths.

patterns.name: Craven's Bonefish Junk
patterns.notes: Rubber legs and hot-orange accent trigger large T&C bones; widely recommended for Bahamas-family destinations including T&C flats.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.notes: Neutral amber profile in sizes #4-#8 works across T&C's varied bottom substrates; recommended as a standard Bahamas-style flat fly by multiple sources.

patterns.name: Christmas Island Special
patterns.notes: Small profile with quiet water entry makes it excellent for the calm, clear conditions on Provo flats and Bottle Creek wading areas.

patterns.name: Del Brown's Permit Fly (Merkin)
patterns.notes: Permit are present on T&C flats, particularly near stingray feeding craters; the Merkin is a standard crab presentation for both permit and crab-feeding bonefish.

patterns.name: Peterson's Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: Effective for both large T&C bonefish and occasional permit; the egg-sac trigger is particularly potent on large, selective bones common on North/Middle Caicos.

patterns.name: EP Ghost Shrimp
patterns.notes: Recommended by Deep Water Cay (Grand Bahama) guides — an identical fishery context to T&C; tan colorway matches Caicos Bank sand-flat shrimp.

patterns.name: Meko Special
patterns.notes: Designed to work across all bottom colors without fly changes — ideal for DIY T&C anglers moving between sand flats, turtle grass, and marl.

patterns.name: Clouser Deep Minnow
patterns.notes: Lead-eye Clouser in tan/white handles the deeper Caicos Bank channels where large bonefish cruise; also takes barracuda and jacks incidentally.

regions.name: Cayman Islands
regions.notes: Grand Cayman has the largest bonefish (averaging 3-5 lb) and a certified guide industry (Fish-Bones, Fish Cayman). Little Cayman has numerous but smaller bones (averaging 2-4 lb). The turtle grass and mixed-bottom flats demand weedless flies. Grand Cayman also offers tarpon, snook, and occasional permit. The fish are described as pressured and having 'seen every Gotcha and Crazy Charlie' — finesse, locally developed patterns excel.

patterns.name: The Usual
patterns.notes: Grand Cayman guide service Fish-Bones' signature fly, featured in Dick Brown's Bonefish Fly Patterns; derived from Veverka Mantis Shrimp and optimized for Cayman turtle-grass flats with short-twitch retrieve.

patterns.name: Simple Shrimp
patterns.notes: Heavier companion to The Usual, designed for a defensive splayed-leg posture on the bottom; rust with orange tail is the top Cayman tailing-bonefish color.

patterns.name: Cayman Sleek
patterns.notes: Pearl mylar body, golden bead-chain eyes, brown/tan craft-fur tail, rubber legs; developed specifically after Cayman bonefish refused standard Gotchas and Crazy Charlies — effective on both small and large fish across size range.

patterns.name: Hot-Legs Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Cayman-specific variant of the Crazy Charlie with orange-tipped rubber legs for mixed sand-and-grass flats; sparse body ensures fast sink and soft landing.

patterns.name: Strip Tease (Sparkplug)
patterns.notes: Recommended by Fish-Bones for deep 'white holes' on flood tides when Cayman bones key on sand-fleas and crabs; semi-translucent UV body with rubber legs and orange mouth.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Foundation pattern used on all three Cayman islands; the Hot-Legs variant is preferred locally, but the standard Charlie remains a reliable fallback on cooperative fish.

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.notes: Cayman fish have seen heavy Gotcha pressure on guided flats; still effective on fresh fish and in deeper water where presentation distance reduces spooking.

patterns.name: Veverka Mantis Shrimp
patterns.notes: The parent pattern of Fish-Bones' The Usual — bead-chain eyes provide gentle landing for pressured Cayman bones tailing in shallow turtle grass.

patterns.name: Gartside Gurgler
patterns.notes: Fish-Bones lists a Gurgler as a top Cayman tarpon and snook fly; the Central Mangrove Wetlands and shoreline cuts on Grand Cayman hold both species.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.notes: Proven neutral profile for pressured flats fish; amber version mimics the common snapping shrimp found on Cayman grass flats.

patterns.name: Clouser Deep Minnow
patterns.notes: Lead-eye Fox-and-Bunny Clouser variant is the Fish-Bones go-to for deeper water cruising bones; also targets Cayman tarpon and cuda in channels.

patterns.name: Lefty's Deceiver
patterns.notes: Standard cuda and tarpon baitfish presentation for Cayman reef edges; the Fish-Bones site confirms barracuda and tarpon as key Cayman species alongside bonefish.

regions.name: ABC Islands (Bonaire, Aruba, Curaçao)
regions.notes: Bonaire is the star — Sorobon lagoon and Lac Bay are ankle-to-knee-deep DIY flats with clear water and mixed sand-and-weed bottom. Fishing Adventures Bonaire (Peter Tuinman) confirms permit, barracuda, jacks, cubera snapper, ladyfish, tripletail, and tarpon alongside bones. The DIY scene rewards simple, easy-to-tie patterns that can be self-supplied. Rocky, hard-bottom sections near coral require weed guards.

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.notes: The most recommended DIY bonefish fly worldwide; tan and pearl variants in #4-#6 with varied bead-chain weight are the essential Bonaire flat staple.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Easy to tie and widely available; ideal for DIY anglers self-supplying flies for Bonaire — multiple color and weight variants cover all Lac Bay conditions.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.notes: Soft-hackle neutral-profile shrimp excellent for cautious Bonaire bones on clear, calm lagoon flats; amber body mimics common Caribbean mantis shrimp coloration.

patterns.name: Veverka Mantis Shrimp
patterns.notes: Soft entry and realistic mantis shrimp silhouette suit Bonaire's clear, calm Sorobon-lagoon conditions where sight-fishing is the norm.

patterns.name: EP Ghost Shrimp
patterns.notes: Tan EP Ghost Shrimp in #6-#8 with bead-chain eyes is well-suited to Bonaire's crystal-clear water and mixed-sand flats; sparse profile avoids spooking fish in gin-clear conditions.

patterns.name: Christmas Island Special
patterns.notes: Quiet entry, small profile, and versatile gold/orange colorway suit the calm Bonaire lagoon conditions; easy to tie for DIY fly tyers preparing for the trip.

patterns.name: Clouser Deep Minnow
patterns.notes: Lead-eye Clouser covers deeper Lac Bay edges and channel margins; also the most versatile choice for barracuda and jacks frequently encountered by wading anglers.

patterns.name: Del Brown's Permit Fly (Merkin)
patterns.notes: Permit are confirmed on Bonaire flats (Fishing Adventures Bonaire); Merkin crab on a sinking presentation is the standard approach when permit are spotted.

patterns.name: Borski Slider
patterns.notes: Deerhair head with rabbit strip tail creates a sliding action through the water; confirmed effective for both bonefish and the jack crevalle encountered on Bonaire flats.

patterns.name: Lefty's Deceiver
patterns.notes: Versatile baitfish pattern for the barracuda, tarpon (occasionally), and jack crevalle that share Bonaire's lagoons and reef edges with bonefish.

patterns.name: Peterson's Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: Rabbit-fur wing provides natural pulse on shallow weed flats; effective on sight-feeding Bonaire bonefish and carries the egg-sac trigger that consistently produces multiple-fish days.

patterns.name: Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: Widely cited as a tournament-winning bonefish pattern across the Caribbean; the realistic spawning shrimp profile is effective in the prolific crustacean habitat of Bonaire's mangrove-fringed lagoons.

regions.name: Boca Paila & Sian Ka'an, Mexico
regions.notes: Distinct from Ascension Bay and Espíritu Santo Bay to the south. Boca Paila Lagoon and the northern Sian Ka'an flats include Caampechen, San Miguel, and the immediate Boca Paila zone. Bonefish, permit (palometa), baby/juvenile tarpon, snook in mangrove cuts, barracuda, and jacks. Founded 1964, Boca Paila Lodge set the standard for flats fishing. Mixed sand, turtle grass, and marl bottoms; clear to slightly turbid water. Mexico Yucatan permit are famously difficult. Snook in mangrove creeks respond to surface flies. Baby tarpon in lagoon channels.

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.notes: Standard flat-fly across all Yucatan bonefish venues; tan, pearl, and pink variants in #4-#8 with bead-chain eyes are the reliable first choice for Boca Paila bonefish.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.notes: Xcalak and Boca Paila guides consistently recommend Crazy Charlie in tan and pearl for Yucatan bonefish on both sandy and grassy bottoms.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.notes: Top choice for Yucatan bones in sizes #6-#8 per Xcalak-area guides; a touch of orange or pink hotspot in the tan version performs especially well.

patterns.name: Del Brown's Permit Fly (Merkin)
patterns.notes: The original crab pattern for Mexico's palometa (permit); standard at Boca Paila Lodge and throughout the Sian Ka'an for tailing permit on grass flats.

patterns.name: Flexo Crab
patterns.notes: Xcalak-area guides list Flexo Crab as a top permit pattern for Sian Ka'an flats; olive, tan, and white in #2-#4 with rubber legs and quick sink rate.

patterns.name: Strong Arm Merkin
patterns.notes: Recommended by Xcalak guides for Yucatan permit; natural-color crab with rubber legs sinks quickly to meet tailing permit before they move off the flat.

patterns.name: Tarpon Toad
patterns.notes: Black-and-purple Tarpon Toad in 1/0 is a primary pattern for the juvenile tarpon (baby tarpon) that roll in Boca Paila Lagoon channels and mangrove cuts.

patterns.name: Black Death
patterns.notes: Classic black-and-purple tarpon/snook streamer; recommended by Xcalak and Sian Ka'an guides for baby tarpon in low-light and tannic mangrove water.

patterns.name: Gartside Gurgler
patterns.notes: Surface gurgler is extremely effective for Boca Paila snook ambushing baitfish along mangrove edges and for juvenile tarpon in the Sian Ka'an lagoon channels.

patterns.name: Lefty's Deceiver
patterns.notes: White/chartreuse Deceiver is a standard snook and barracuda pattern for Boca Paila mangrove channels and lagoon drop-offs; also takes juvenile tarpon.

patterns.name: Peterson's Spawning Shrimp
patterns.notes: Effective for both Boca Paila bonefish and permit; the spawning-shrimp trigger is especially relevant in spring and early summer when Caribbean shrimp spawn on Sian Ka'an flats.

patterns.name: Christmas Island Special
patterns.notes: Gold and orange variants are recommended for Mexican Yucatan bonefish in shallow, calm conditions; the unweighted or plastic-eye version lands softly on spooky flats.

patterns.name: EP Backcountry Baitfish
patterns.notes: EP fiber baitfish in white/chartreuse or olive/white is a premier snook and backcountry species pattern for Boca Paila's mangrove-creek and lagoon environments.
